content: Continued fractions are most effectively taught via the square-filling-rectangle method (NRICH, Robert Dickau, adamponting.com, Wolfram Demonstrations all converge on this): start with a rectangle sized to the fraction, repeatedly cut off the largest square, count squares cut at each stage = partial quotients, and the final square's side = GCD (directly visualizing Euclid's algorithm geometrically). Fibonacci ratios produce near-golden spirals, a visually striking special case. Distinct from this, dedicated calculators (dCode, monocalc, agentcalc) separately show a convergents table (numerator/denominator/decimal approx/error) with a terms slider.
